quote: a wise man, if indeed it be proper to call him a man
summary: Eusebius introduces the Testimonium 'in the same work' immediately after quoting the John the Baptist passage, and gives it in essentially the extant form, including 'He was the Christ'. This is the earliest surviving quotation of it.
limits: McGiffert's translation of 1890; the NPNF page does not give Eusebius's Greek. Eusebius also quotes the passage in the Demonstratio Evangelica 3.5 and the Theophany (named in Hillar's essay; neither opened here). Verifier: Olson and Carrier (other candidates) argue Eusebius may be the Testimonium's author, so this is the earliest quotation but not independent evidence that Josephus wrote it. Section 7 of HE 1.11 on the page; the quote and the lead-in 'in the same work' confirmed.
